title: A blessing from the Highlands
hookLine: Carmina Gadelica: a blessing for kindling the fire each morning
tomorrow: how do you tell your own story without making yourself the hero?

lines: THE FIRST THOUGHT, BEFORE YOU'RE UP.
cards: The morning after something goes wrong, the first thought can arrive before you're out of bed: the mistake, the clip, the name of whoever laughed. In a Highland house in Scotland, the first job of the morning was smaller.
Light the fire. And it came with words. Alexander Carmichael wrote one such blessing down in his collection, Carmina Gadelica.
Read it slowly, because halfway through, the fire it's talking about changes.

teach.b: In Carmichael's English, the speaker kindles the fire this morning in the presence of the holy angels of heaven.

Then comes a list of what stays out: without malice, without jealousy, without envy, without fear of anyone under the sun, with the Holy Son of God as shield. Before any wood catches, the heart is cleared.
Notice that the blessing names those feelings. It doesn't pretend they aren't in the room. It sets them outside the door before the work starts.
The speaker asks God to kindle a flame of love in the heart within. And that flame has a guest list: to my neighbor, to my foe, to my friend, to my kindred all. The brave, the knave, the thrall.
From the lowliest thing that lives up to the Name that is highest of all.
Here's the detail worth repeating: the foe stands right beside the friend, in one line, before breakfast. That's the Sermon on the Mount carried into a kitchen.
Jesus says, “Love your enemies, bless them that curse you.”

And a fire is a fitting picture for it. Two disciples on the road to Emmaus, once they knew who had walked beside them, said: “Did not our heart burn within us?” The fire in the grate warms one room for a day.
The fire the blessing asks for is meant to reach everyone the day brings, the hard ones too.

how: Carmina Gadelica, collected by Alexander Carmichael, gives blessings for daily work in the Scottish Highlands and islands; some Christians today read them at the start of household tasks.

games.q: what does “a blessing from the highlands” mean?
o: a farewell for emigrants sailing away from Scotland
a Scottish war song sung before a clan battle
a Gaelic prayer for lighting the morning fire with love

games.q: what's in the blessing — tap the pairs.

s: the kindling blessing asks God to keep the speaker's enemies away
it asks for a flame of love to neighbor, foe and friend alike.
blessing a foe means pretending they did nothing wrong
the blessing calls them a foe. it just puts them on the guest list for love.
Carmina Gadelica gathers blessings for everyday work
kindling the fire among them, from the Highlands and islands of Scotland.

games.q: your brother's friend embarrassed him at practice. next morning he's making toast and muttering about payback. what does the Highland blessing give him?
o: a reason to avoid that friend from now on, quietly.
a way to start: set malice down, and put the friend in the flame too.
a promise that God will settle the score for him.
games.why: the blessing names malice and envy and sets them outside before the fire is lit, then asks for love to neighbor, foe and friend.

practice: Choose the first ordinary task waiting for you: the kettle, the stove, the inbox, the drive. As you begin it, or as you plan to, set down malice, envy and fear one at a time, the way the blessing does, before the work starts.
If someone feels like a foe today, hold their name for a moment beside a friend's.

wordCard.voice: A blessing from the Highlands. A Gaelic prayer for lighting the morning fire that asks for a flame of love in the heart too.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: kindle the fire. A flame for the stove, and one for the foe. See you tomorrow.
